result.title: New Model, Old Habits: Behavior Transfer under Model Swapping in Multi-Session LLM Agents
result.summary: Multi-session agents can switch between LLMs to balance performance and inference cost. Such switches require transferring a history for continuity, yet their effects on the recipient remain underexplored. Through controlled experiments with multi-session tasks, we uncover behavior transfer: recipients tend to adopt reasoning and action patterns from the models that generated their histories. This effect is most evident with raw-history transfer but is substantially reduced by summarization. Based on these findings, we propose Direction- and Authorship-aware Summarization of History (DASH) that preserves stronger-model behavior while minimizing weak-to-strong transfer via summarization. Experiments with repeated swaps show that DASH outperforms raw-history transfer and naive summarization baselines. These results suggest that effective multi-model orchestration requires considering not only which model to use, but also which behavioral patterns to carry forward.

AI.brief_summary: 通过多会话任务的受控实验发现，模型切换后接收方会继承历史生成模型的推理与动作模式，并据此提出方向与作者感知的历史摘要方法 DASH，以保留强模型行为、抑制弱到强的行为迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 「原史直接迁移」与「摘要」造成的行为迁移差异，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态或轨迹应保留何种推理信息、如何分配监督贡献提供可核查线索；但对象为纯文本多会话智能体，与视觉推理无直接关联。
